## Historical audit — S0098, visible chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/external_followup/scene_rsi_pilot/selected/external_followup/bw_0011/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file; the supplied observations of these lines are complete, so no split offsets apply.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 | The stated goal was an editable reconstruction of a clean-laboratory corner: blue seamed walls, coved floor, suspended ceiling and exposed services, glazed cabinet, botanical mural and digital display. The fixed runner, not the program, controlled saving and rendering. The reference image itself is not visible to this audit. |
| Initial construction — student response and execution, lines 3–4 | The program constructed multiple named owners for architecture, cabinet, mural, display, ceiling and services. It specified cabinet doors, shelves and handles, a seven-strip cove, wall-mounted features, a 32 mm camera, LED emitters and an additional entrance light. It used procedural noise and filament geometry for the mural, plus scoped steel/glass shader settings. These are code operations, not independent proof of visible objects, correct connections, support, pose or material appearance. |
| Validation — execution result and selections, lines 5–7 | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, completed 16 samples and logged saving a PNG and `scene.blend`; step 1 was selected twice. This establishes an operational output, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Autonomous revision — student request, response and execution, lines 8–11 | Given the render and a request to compare it, the student estimated several reference/render anchor discrepancies and judged several surfaces too pale. Those are student visual hypotheses, not audit-verified measurements. It chose an illumination/world revision, reducing world strength, LED and entrance power and diffuser emission, and added a camera-ray white background. It also changed door construction to retain the node returned by `include`, so the code was not strictly appearance-only. The camera parameters remained unchanged. |
| Second validation — execution result and selections, lines 12–14 | Step 2 also reported `ok: true`, completed 16 samples and logged a PNG and blend save; step 2 was selected twice. No image comparison or formal evaluation of that revision is visible here. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher event or teacher-specific advice is visible in this chunk. The follow-up comparison and scheduling instructions were delivered as user messages in the student request (line 8); the subsequent response demonstrably used the reported elapsed time and made a comparison-driven revision (line 10). This does not establish receipt or adoption of any separate teacher input.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Two builds succeeded operationally; overall correctness and final outcome are **unknown**, not formal success or algorithm failure. The student itself left camera/edge and anchor discrepancies unresolved (line 10). Actual visibility, occlusion, contacts and composite editability, texture/material distinction, lighting improvement, and fidelity of the room and object poses require image and structural checks unavailable in this audit. The unseen second chunk may contain later events; none are inferred.

**Lessons:** Transferably, separate execution success from visual and structural verification, and treat proposed lighting fixes as hypotheses until compared. Here, the particular pale-surface diagnosis and lighting values are task-specific, unverified hypotheses; the extra entrance light also differs from the request for LED-only illumination.
